**Fixes a freeze in v0.6.3.** Moving many files on a drive could lock up
the drive and the file manager using it, until Windows was restarted.
Update from v0.6.3 straight away.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `cloak-v0.6.4-windows-x64.zip` | [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev) (`winget install WinFsp.WinFsp`) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `cloak-v0.6.4-macos-arm64.dmg` | [macFUSE](https://macfuse.github.io) |

**Windows:** unzip and run `Cloak\Cloak.exe`. Keep the folder together: the
engine is in `Cloak\bin`, and your drive list and settings are kept in
`Cloak\cloak-data`.

**macOS:** open the disk image and drag **Cloak** onto **Applications**. The
app isn't notarized, so before opening it the first time, clear the download
quarantine: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Cloak.app` (or
right-click Cloak → Open, then Open again). macFUSE's kernel extension must be
allowed; on Apple Silicon that means its one-time Reduced Security setup.

## Fixed

- **v0.6.3 could freeze a drive while files were being moved.** Its new
  notices for the folder an item was moved out of hit a deadlock in WinFsp
  2.1's driver when several moves came close together. The drive and the
  program moving the files then stopped responding, and that program couldn't
  be ended until Windows was restarted. This release takes that change back
  out, so the mount driver is the same as v0.6.2's.

  If v0.6.3 froze for you, restart Windows, then install this version. Your
  files are safe; a file moved just before the freeze may show up back in its
  old folder.

## Known limitations

- **A folder an item is moved out of may need a refresh (F5)** before it
  stops showing the item, as in v0.6.2. A fix that avoids the deadlock is
  being tested.
- Auto-lock runs on sleep, not when the screen locks.
- The app isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run
  (More info → Run anyway).
- The middle of every file stays plaintext on disk by design.
- Hidden files of the same drive can be shown to belong together (they share
  the lock's salt); a file on its own looks random.
